purpose: Quinapril is mainly used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension), which helps lower your risk of heart attack and stroke. It is also used to treat heart failure. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and blood vessels.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that tightens your blood vessels and raises blood pressure. Quinapril blocks the enzyme that makes this chemical, so your blood vessels relax and widen. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down.
common_side_effects: A dry, nagging cough is the most common side effect — it happens in some people and does not go away on its own. You may also feel dizzy, especially when you stand up quickly, or feel tired. Some people notice headache or mild nausea.
warnings: Do NOT take quinapril if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you notice swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, as this can be a rare but dangerous reaction called angioedema. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially potassium supplements or potassium-sparing diuretics, as your potassium levels could rise too high. Avoid taking it with aliskiren if you have diabetes.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 10 mg once a day. Your doctor may adjust it to between 20 mg and 80 mg per day, taken once or split into two doses. For heart failure, the starting dose is usually lower, around 5 mg twice a day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
